articles.title: Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic hit $16.8 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 45 percent gain that still falls far short of Q2's 140 percent surge. With a November IPO approaching, some investors now expect the company's valuation to drop below $1.5 trillion. Slowing growth and a tough market are cooling expectations for the AI boom's biggest Wall Street test yet. The article Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Matthias Bastian

articles.title: Anthropic Urged to Pause IPO for AI Safety by NYC Comptroller
articles.summary: Anthropic should pause its initial public offering until it has fully addressed risks around artificial intelligence, according to New York City’s comptroller. A letter from Mark Levine addressed to Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei on Wednesday suggested the Claude developer should instead focus on addressing the unprecedented risks of the technology. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Santander's Ana Botin on US Growth, Debt, AI and the Global Economy | The David Rubenstein Show
articles.summary: Santander Executive Chair Ana Botin sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss the bank's expansion in the US, including its recent acquisition of Webster Financial, and why she sees lack of economic growth as one of the biggest challenges facing the global economy. She also discusses US debt, the outlook for the US and European economies amid geopolitical uncertainty, and the impact of AI on banking and jobs. Botin is on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This episode was recorded July 13 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Ramp Completes Funding at $60 Billion Value as Revenue Surges
articles.summary: Ramp has surged to $2 billion in annualized revenue, the fintech company plans to announce Thursday — a milestone that’s helped attract fresh investor capital.

articles.title: SmartNews Said to Plan December Tokyo IPO as Valuation Craters
articles.summary: SmartNews Inc. is planning an initial public offering in December at a fraction of its previous valuation, according to people familiar with the matter, a sign of the news aggregator’s business being decimated by artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Nvidia, Anthropic Weigh In On AI Safeguards
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he would halt the supply of chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software, though he doesn’t believe that the current level of concern about the technology is warranted. AI executives such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have proposed an industrywide slowdown to address the concerns. Meantime, Anthropic held an investor day Wednesday as it advances plans for a potential IPO at an approximately $2 trillion valuation, amid growing concerns about AI safety and threats. We get reaction from Bloomberg Tech host Ed Ludlow & Jacqueline Corbelli, Co-Founder and CEO at Brightline Partners. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Inflation Rises as Fuel Costs Surge
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Inflation heats up as fuel prices risev and Middle East tensions threaten more pressure ahead. Big bank earnings expose a divide on Wall Street. RBC’s Gerard Cassidy breaks down rates, margins and credit risk. Plus, AI demand keeps surging. Stripe Vice Chair Eileen O’Mara on Europe’s startup push and how agentic commerce could transform payments. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: PSP’s Momei Qu on Anthropic’s Pre-IPO Investor Day
articles.summary: Ahead of Anthropic’s pre-IPO investor day, Momei Qu of PSP Growth says public-market investors may disagree over whether fast-growing AI companies deserve lower margins and heavy capital spending—or must prove stronger returns and profitability. Recent IPO setbacks, including a collapse in Asia and Aura’s withdrawal, illustrate the uncertainty facing both AI firms beyond Anthropic and companies outside the sector. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO The phrase "told investors" appears four times in this FT article, which reports on Anthropic's day of hosting investors on Wednesday. Lots of details in here from "people with knowledge of the matter". Key things I learned from the article: Q1 revenue (Jan/Feb/Mar) was "about $4.8bn" Q2 (Apr/May/Jun) was $11.5bn Q3 (Jul/Aug/Sep) was $16.8bn In Q3: $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on "computing power" Adjusted operating margins (excluding stock-based compensation) were 11% This point about distillation is worth quoting in full (highlight mine): The start-up has also clamped down on “distillation” — a controversial practice whereby rival AI labs train their models on the outputs of more advanced ones. When rival companies “distil” their models from Anthropic’s models, that involves heavy usage and spending. articles.title: Banks Poised to Surprise Wall Street: Analyst
articles.summary: Baird Senior Research Analyst David George joins Bloomberg Open Interest to lay out why he’s bullish on upcoming bank earnings despite a risk‑off market. He explains how AI-driven capital markets may cool, why regional banks could outperform the Wall Street giants, and how post‑election consolidation and higher rates set up JPMorgan and others for upside this quarter. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: T-Mobile Rises on Upgrade; IonQ to Buy Elisity | Stock Movers
articles.summary: On this episode of Stock Movers: - Amazon (AMZN) shares are moving on news it's in negotiations to acquire Decart AI, an artificial intelligence startup, in a deal that could be valued at around $7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported. The purchase could be wrapped up soon if the negotiations don’t collapse, the Journal said, citing people familiar with the matter. - IonQ (IONQ) shares are moving after it agreed to buy Elisity for as much as $1.3 billion in an all-stock transaction to expand its cybersecurity platform. IonQ Chief Executive Officer Niccolo de Masi said the company will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era. - T-Mobile (TMUS) shares are rising after Raymond James upgraded the stock to outperform from market perform, noting that the recent pullback in shares has created a buying opportunity. (Source: Bloomberg)
